passage:
Tuesday night, very tired.
All week I have been checking where Hafsa sits: the bus, the lunch bench, the art table. Today she sat with Tanvi again. I asked her why three times. Her face went tight and she said, "Nitin, you are everywhere." My ears burned.
Then I finally said the true thing: "I feel left out. Can we do one thing just us?"
She was quiet, then said, "Saturday, cycling?"
I am still a little scared she will like Tanvi more. But my stomach does not hurt as much now. 🙂
- Nitin

qa.q: Where did Hafsa suggest going with Nitin on Saturday?
What was Nitin afraid of all week?
qa.a: Nitin was afraid of being replaced by Tanvi, so he kept checking where Hafsa sat.

qa.q: What worked better than checking where she sits?
qa.a: Telling her plainly about feeling left out and asking for one plan just for them worked better, since checking made her feel trapped.

qa.q: How might Hafsa have felt when Nitin asked three times?
qa.a: She felt crowded and a bit trapped, which showed in her tight face and her words, "you are everywhere."

grounding: A child fears being replaced, checks who a friend sits with, then says they feel left out and asks for one plan just for the two of them.

passage:
"Varun, sit. Your Himani Masi once nearly lost her best friend by holding on too tight. In Class 5, Chitra started doing homework with a new girl after school. I was terrified she'd forget me. So I watched her. Every morning: 'Who did you sit with? Why?' I even said, 'If you're really my friend, don't talk to her at lunch.'
One day Chitra snapped, 'It's like I'm in a cage with you!' and walked off.
That night I wrote down what I actually felt. Next day I told her, 'I feel left out. Can Sundays be just us?' She hugged me. We still speak every Sunday."

qa.q: What did young Himani ask Chitra every morning?
qa.a: She asked, "Who did you sit with? Why?"

qa.q: What was young Himani afraid of when Chitra made a new friend?
qa.a: She was terrified of being replaced and forgotten, which is why she watched Chitra and tested her loyalty.

qa.q: Which choice in the story helped, and why?
qa.a: Telling Chitra plainly "I feel left out" and asking for Sundays just together, because it asked for time without controlling who Chitra could talk to.

qa.q: How did Himani's checking and testing feel to Chitra?
qa.a: Chitra felt trapped, saying it was like being in a cage, and she walked off.

grounding: An aunt recalls fearing her best friend would replace her, clinging and testing her loyalty until the friend felt trapped, then saying plainly she felt left out and asking for one plan together.

passage:
This year Parveen was put in section B, and Joseph stayed in A. They only had the fifteen-minute break together, and on Monday Parveen spent it with Mehak from her new class.
By Thursday Joseph was waiting outside section B before the bell. "Who are you sitting with? Is it Mehak again?" He followed her to the tap and back.
Parveen stopped. "Joseph, you're like a guard. I can't even breathe."
Joseph's face went hot. He walked away and kicked a stone. At home he practised the words.
Friday he said, "I feel left out since you moved. Could we cycle on Saturday, just us?"
Parveen nodded. "Yes. I miss that too."

qa.q: Which section was Parveen put in this year?
qa.a: She was put in section B.

qa.q: What was Joseph afraid of when he waited outside section B?
qa.a: He was afraid Mehak would replace him as Parveen's friend, and that fear made him cling and check on her.

qa.q: What did Joseph change that worked better?
qa.a: He stopped checking and said plainly that he felt left out, then asked for one plan together: cycling on Saturday.

qa.q: How did Joseph's checking feel to Parveen?
qa.a: She felt watched and trapped, telling him he was like a guard and she could not breathe.

grounding: A boy afraid of being replaced clings to his best friend and checks who she sits with; she feels trapped, and he then tells her plainly he feels left out and asks for one plan together.
